question: Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks are included in which measure of money supply?
solution:
The correct answer is** **__**M2.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• 
 The total stock of money of all types (currency and demand deposits) held by the people of a country at a given point in time is referred to as the **money supply.**
 
 
• 
 Money supply can be measured in a variety of ways, including **M1, M2, M3, **and **M4 **measurements.
 
 
• 
 Every measurement has its own definition, with various components **ranging **from the **most liquid **to the **most rigid**.
 
 
• 
 Savings deposits at post office savings banks are included in the **M2 measurement **of money supply in India, making it a little more rigid than the** M1 measurement.**
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• Money supply is defined as the **total amount **of **currency **that can be included in a country's economy.
 
• The total money supply includes both **cash **and **deposits **that can be** ****easily converted **into **cash**.
 
• Money supply economics is associated with **direct government **power because it is the government that issues currency, either in paper form or as a coin, as a combination of treasury bills and bank demand draughts.
 
• Similarly, **banks **have **influence **over the **money supply**, which they exercise through **reserves **and **credit controls**.
 
• Money supply has a significant **impact **on a **country's economy**.
